ideas.title: Two-valued (Kummer) bucket gain: exact multiset filters on {h(P+Q),h(P-Q)}
ideas.statement: KN-OPEN-91d4f6 defines G(M) with a single-valued combining rule f. But S_3 makes the unordered pair {x(P+Q),x(P-Q)} an exact algebraic function of (x(P),x(Q)), so a filter h on x has an exact 2-valued rule f2:[M]^2 -> multisets of size 2 whenever h factors through symmetric functions of the pair. Define G2(M)=(M/2)*max_{c,d,e} Pr[{h(P+Q),h(P-Q)}={d,e} | h(P),h(Q)=c-pattern] and ask whether a Wagner tree on the Kummer line (x-only, sign-ambiguous legs, 2^t branch blow-up per depth t) can have G2 growing.
ideas.mechanism: Replace group-quotient filters by filters on the Kummer line P^1=E/<-1>, where addition is a 2-valued correspondence given by S_3. A k-tree whose merges are 2-valued pays factor 2 per level but filters with an exact algebraic relation rather than a group homomorphism.
ideas.wall_bypassed:
Wagner/k-list wall (no small visible quotient of E(F_q)) and Theorem C of KN-FIND-ffe1df (no exact single-valued filter on

).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Both statements quantify over single-valued maps h with h(Q+R)=f(h(Q),h(R)); a 2-valued correspondence on P^1 is not a homomorphism to a quotient group, so the no-quotient argument does not cover it.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Only if some h with M=l^theta buckets has G2(M) -> infinity: then each Wagner level gains M^{theta'} at 2x branch cost and the tree depth log k gives a sub-sqrt rate. The honest expectation: the only exact 2-valued rules are those with h = identity on x (M=p), giving no compression; any h with M << p mixes pairs uniformly (Weil bound on the S_3 curve fibred over buckets), so G2=O(1). Then it is a theory/closure item.
ideas.prior_art: Semaev 2004 summation polynomials; KN-FIND-ffe1df (Theorem C); Wagner 2002; Kummer-line arithmetic (Montgomery ladder pseudo-addition, which is exactly the 3-point rule x(P+Q) from x(P),x(Q),x(P-Q)).

falsifier.design: Binary curves n=13,15,17,19 (prime-order subgroup), F_2-linear filters h=(Tr(a_1 x),...,Tr(a_j x)), j=2..8, 200 random (a_i) plus the best found by greedy search; also prime-field p~2^20 with h=x mod M and h=floor(x M/p). Exhaust all pairs (Q,R) in a 2^12 sample of legs per bucket; compute G2(M) and the single-valued G(M) for comparison.
falsifier.toy_params: n in {13,15,17,19}; j in 2..8; 2^12 legs per bucket; prime p ~ 2^20, M in {4..256}
falsifier.prediction_if_true: max G2(M) grows with n at fixed j/n (e.g. >=2x from n=13 to 19) and exceeds the permutation null by >5 sigma.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: G2(M) = 1+O(M/sqrt(sample)) uniformly, matching G(M); closes the 2-valued extension of KN-OPEN-91d4f6 for linear filters.

ideas.risk: high probability of null; value is in extending the open problem's closure to multi-valued rules.

ideas.title: Bourgain-Glibichuk-Konyagin certification of the chord ceiling for multiplicative-subgroup x-bases
ideas.statement: THM_INCBARRIER1/2 leave gap G1: the chord-richness ceiling T_3 ~ generic mean cannot be certified for fixed F below B=p^{2/3} by Weil sums, and Theorem C says moment methods stop at alpha=1/2. For F = {P : x(P) in H}, H < F_p^* a multiplicative subgroup of size p^delta, BGK/Bourgain exponential-sum bounds over subgroups give power savings for every delta>0. Claim: the T_3 deviation for subgroup bases is bounded by B^2 p^{-eps(delta)} unconditionally, i.e. the cross-x sign cancellation statement F holds for subgroup bases, closing them as structured factor bases in all ranges alpha>0.
ideas.mechanism: Write T_3 via the chord profile identity (THM_INCBARRIER2) as a sum over x in H of delta(x); expand the indicator of H by multiplicative characters of index (p-1)/|H|; the cross terms are mixed additive-multiplicative sums over the S_3 surface restricted to H x H, bounded by Bourgain's sum-product exponential-sum estimate for subgroups.
ideas.wall_bypassed: The Theorem C barrier (norm/moment family cannot cross alpha=1/2) in THM_INCBARRIER2 and the Weil limit B=Omega(p^{2/3}).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Theorem C bounds methods using only profile moments of a generic F; a subgroup base carries multiplicative structure that sum-product estimates exploit, which is outside the moment family.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None as an attack: this is an obstruction theorem (structured subgroup bases have generic yield). It is useful as the first unconditional ceiling below alpha=1/2, and it says which side lever 6 (mu_263 bases) lands on in the prime-field analogue.
ideas.prior_art: Bourgain-Glibichuk-Konyagin 2006; Bourgain 2005 'Mordell's exponential sum estimate revisited'; Shparlinski on elliptic-curve character sums over subgroups; THM_INCBARRIER1/2 (programme); 'Uniform sum-product phenomenon for algebraic groups' arXiv 2603.06483.

falsifier.design: Prime p in [2^20,2^24] with p-1 having divisors giving |H| = p^delta, delta in {0.25,0.3,0.35,0.4,0.45}; random curves y^2=x^3+ax+b; F = lifts of x in H; compute T_3 exactly via hash of x(P+Q) for all pairs, compare to mu~ = BT/(6L)-d/3; fit log|T_3-mu~|/log B. Controls: random x-sets of equal size; x-intervals of equal size.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: |T_3-mu~| <= B^{2-eps} with eps>0 stable across p for subgroups (deviation exponent <= that of random sets) at delta<1/2.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Subgroup bases show deviation exponent near 2 (T_3 excess ~ B^2/p^{small}) at some delta, i.e. a structured base with super-generic chord count; that would be an advance candidate for prime-field yield variance.

ideas.risk: Proof may need mixed sums over a curve, not a line; Bourgain's estimates for curves exist only partially.

ideas.title: Group-Fourier spectrum of structured factor bases: Bohr-set yield variance
ideas.statement:
Number of k-decompositions of R equals (1/r) sum_chi hat(1_F)(chi)^k conj(chi(R)). The monodromy closure fixes the mean yield but leaves variance free; variance = (1/r^2) sum_{chi != 1} |hat(1_F)(chi)|^{2k}. Measure max_{chi!=1}|hat(1_F)(chi)|/B for F defined by x in an F_2-subspace, x in an interval, x in a subgroup, Hamming ball; a large coefficient means F correlates with a Bohr set of

, so decomposability of R+[a]P depends on a in a structured way that a randomised target search could exploit (pick a in the Bohr set).
ideas.mechanism: Exploit spectral non-uniformity of the factor-base indicator on the group; the randomisation offset a is known (not a DL), so if yield(R+[a]P) correlates with chi([a]P)=e(a j/r) for a known large frequency j, choosing a near the peak raises per-trial success.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Summation-cover monodromy (mean yield) closure; free lever 'variance of yield'.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The monodromy closure is about the mean over targets; it states variance is free. Offset choice is a selection over targets whose effect depends on second-order statistics only.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Gain per trial is at most 1 + |hat(1_F)(chi)|^k/(B^k) relative; to change B*D^2 vs N it must grow with n, i.e. F must have a Fourier coefficient of size B^{1-o(1)}, meaning x-structure aligned with a group character. Expected: |hat| ~ sqrt(B) (pseudorandom, Kohel-Shparlinski type bounds), giving O(1) -> constant factor at most; otherwise advance candidate.
ideas.prior_art: Kohel-Shparlinski 2000 (character sums on elliptic curves); Shparlinski 'distribution of points on elliptic curves in subgroups'; Zhang-Wan deep holes of elliptic codes arXiv 2207.12584; t-designs arXiv 2506.00429; restricted sumsets arXiv 2610.14496.

falsifier.design: Binary n=13,15,17 prime-order subgroups (r ~ 2^11..2^16) and prime p ~ 2^16..2^20 with prime order: compute discrete logs of all base points by full table, form indicator on Z/r, FFT, record max nontrivial |hat|/sqrt(B) and top frequencies; then measure k=2,3 yield of R+[a]P for a chosen at peak frequency vs random a.
falsifier.toy_params: n in {13,15,17}, l in {n/3..n/2}; p ~2^16..2^20 with intervals [0,p^0.4], subgroups p^0.4; 50 random bases per shape
falsifier.prediction_if_true: some structured shape has max |hat|/sqrt(B) growing like B^{c}, c>0.1, with peak-chosen offsets raising k=2 yield by a factor growing in n.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: max |hat|/sqrt(B) = O(sqrt(log r)) for all shapes, equal to random-set control; offset selection gives ratio 1 +/- noise. Closes variance-selection for these shapes.

ideas.risk: Computing peaks needs DL of base points, fine at toy scale; exploitation at scale would require knowing the peak frequency without logs (if peaks exist, the question becomes whether they are representation-predictable).

ideas.title: Sum-product amplification: interval x-base with multiplicative filter on legs
ideas.statement: For x(P),x(Q) in an interval I=[0,p^alpha], S_3 gives x(P+Q)+x(P-Q) and x(P+Q)x(P-Q) as rational functions of low height in (x(P),x(Q)): numerators of size ~p^{4alpha}. For alpha<1/4 the pair-symmetric functions are SMALL integers before reduction (no wraparound), so the sum-difference pair inherits archimedean smallness (a height-like structure over F_p, not a global height). Use this to filter at the second Wagner level: legs U=P+Q with x(U) near a root of a small-coefficient quadratic t^2 - s t + q, (s,q) small rationals with denominator (x1-x2)^2.
ideas.mechanism: Archimedean size of S_3 numerators over an interval base: a non-group filter 'x(U)*(x1-x2)^2 mod p has small symmetric functions' that is exactly sum-compatible at level 1 and approximately at level 2 via lattice reduction of (x(U), 1) against small denominators.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Heights wall (sums of small points are not small) applies to global canonical heights on lifts; here the smallness is of F_p-integers of a rational expression, i.e. a pre-reduction size. Also the lattice-reach wall concerns small roots of S_{m+1} in all variables, while this uses level-wise rational reconstruction.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The heights identity concerns ĥ on a lift to Q; it does not constrain the reduced-mod-p rational reconstruction size of x(U) relative to a known denominator. Lattice reach is about the full system; this is a two-level filter, a different object.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Rational reconstruction of x(U) as (s +- sqrt(s^2-4q))/2 with s,q of size p^{4alpha}/p^{2alpha}... needs sqrt and so gives no lattice-small representation unless 4alpha*2 < 1; at level 2 sums of two such U escape the regime (height doubles). Likely it reproduces the JM reach 1/(m(m+1)2^{m-2}) at m=4 (delta=1/80), i.e. a relabelling of the lattice wall. Classified accounting unless measured reach beats 1/80.
ideas.prior_art: Jochemsz-May; Semaev 2004; Petit et al. on prime-field Semaev with small x; Bremner/'Uniform sum-product for algebraic groups' arXiv 2603.06483 (obstruction for interval/digit bases); Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar 2026-10-24.

falsifier.design: p ~ 2^24..2^32, interval base x in [0,p^alpha], alpha in {1/16,1/12,1/10,1/8}; enumerate level-1 sums U=P+Q, record whether x(U)(x1-x2)^2 reduces to small (s,q) via LLL on 2x2 lattice; at level 2 count pairs (U,V) with U+V landing in the interval base, compare with generic expectation |L1|^2 * p^{alpha-1}.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: level-2 hit rate exceeds generic by factor growing with p at alpha>1/80 (i.e. above JM reach).
falsifier.prediction_if_false: excess vanishes once 8*alpha>... matches JM threshold; level-2 hit rate = generic within 10%.

ideas.risk: Most likely a reformulation of the lattice wall.

ideas.title: Szemeredi-Trotter / sum-product kill of linear x-filters over F_p, extended to bilinear (theta-quality) bound
ideas.statement: Use the arbitrary-field Szemeredi-Trotter theorem (arXiv 2609.27023) on the chord configuration {lines through (P,Q), P,Q in F} to bound #{(P,Q) in F^2: ell(x(P+Q)) in one bucket} for an affine filter on x over F_p by B^2/M + B^{3/2-eps}; this supplies a bilinear bound of quality theta that THM_INCBARRIER2 Theorem F names as the certification target (theta in [2/5,7/10]). New relative to the literature-lane suggestion: compute the quality theta achieved and whether it lands inside the harvesting window.
ideas.mechanism: Point-line incidence bound in F_p^2 (Stevens-de Zeeuw / Rudnev-type) applied to the incidence between base points and chord lines; buckets of an affine filter are unions of vertical lines.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Gap G1 in THM_INCBARRIER1 (fixed adversarial F) and Theorem F's missing bilinear estimate.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Weil-sum certification needs B=Omega(p^{2/3}); incidence bounds are nontrivial for B down to p^{~8/15} or lower with arbitrary-field ST, outside the Weil regime.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Obstruction only: proves G(M) = O(1)+o(1) for affine x-bucket filters on prime fields for B >= p^{beta_0}, closing the linear case of KN-OPEN-91d4f6 prime analogue. No attack; constant-factor/theory.
ideas.prior_art: Stevens-de Zeeuw 2017; Rudnev 2018 point-plane incidences; arXiv 2609.27023; THM_INCBARRIER1/2.

falsifier.design: p ~2^20..2^30 (sampled for large p), F random and adversarial (group-AP, interval, subgroup) of size p^beta, beta in 0.3..0.7; filter ell(x)=floor(M x/p) and x mod M, M=2^4..2^10; measure max-bucket count / (B^2/M) and fit exponent of excess; compare to ST-derived bound.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: measured excess exponent <= ST bound exponent for all shapes; max-bucket gain -> 1 as p grows.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: some shape (group-AP expected) exceeds the bound -> bound mis-derived or group-AP structure must be excluded (rank-defect trivial relations).

ideas.risk: Group-AP family saturates; theorem must be stated modulo trivial relations.
